condition: When CT shows multiple discrete hyperdense pulmonary nodules with lower lobe predominance and no upper lobe involvement
action: Inspect bone-window CT slices to confirm intrinsic calcification (Hounsfield >200 HU) and exclude endobronchial or vascular causes by checking for air bronchograms or vessel continuity
limitation: May fail in early ossification before full calcification; unreliable if motion artifact or metal streaks obscure density measurement

condition: When a left hilar opacity silhouettes the left heart border on PA CXR and lobe localization is ambiguous
action: Inspect lateral view for posterior location and vertical position relative to carina; if lateral unavailable, assume lower lobe until proven otherwise
limitation: Inconclusive if lateral view overpenetrated or obscured; does not assess margin morphology

condition: In post-lobectomy CXRs showing new or worsening ipsilateral opacification, when lobar identity is ambiguous due to absent fissures
action: Inspect for focal convex opacity with medial/ventral displacement relative to prior image and absence of expected volume loss—suggesting torsion rather than atelectasis or fluid
limitation: Fails if overpenetration obscures lobar contours; does not distinguish torsion from mucus plugging with air trapping without clinical correlation

condition: When a new unilateral hemithorax opacity appears after resolution of prior ipsilateral opacity, and mediastinal shift is toward the new opacity
action: Inspect for loss of lung volume (flattened diaphragm, crowding of ribs, tracheal deviation) and absence of meniscus sign to favor atelectasis over effusion
limitation: Fails if poor inspiration or overpenetration masks volume loss; does not differentiate mucus plugging from tumor/foreign body without clinical data

condition: When CXR shows a new unilateral upper/mid-lung opacity in a patient with electrical injury and no trauma/surgery, and the opacity abuts the hilum without diaphragmatic silhouetting
action: Inspect for loss of hilar silhouette (silhouette sign) and absence of meniscus or visceral pleural line; assess for air bronchograms to favor consolidation over atelectasis or effusion
limitation: Fails if overpenetration obscures subtle opacities or if lateral view unavailable; cannot distinguish infection from thermal injury without clinical context

condition: When mediastinal opacity obscures one heart border and tracheal deviation is present on PA CXR
action: Inspect which cardiac border is silhouetted (left border loss = left mediastinal pathology; right border loss = right-sided) and confirm tracheal deviation direction—deviation away from mass side—and compare costophrenic angle blunting severity per side.
limitation: Unreliable if both borders obscured or in severe cardiomegaly; requires adequate inspiration and centering.

condition: When PA CXR shows enlarged central pulmonary arteries and cardiomegaly with right heart border prominence, and symptoms suggest chronic dyspnea
action: Inspect lateral CXR for convex retrosternal clear space and posterior displacement of heart—signs of right ventricular hypertrophy—and exclude left-sided volume overload signs (e.g., upper lobe vessel redistribution, Kerley B lines)
limitation: Unreliable in poor inspiration or scoliosis; does not differentiate etiology of PH (e.g., sarcoid vs. IPAH)

condition: When a well-circumscribed thoracic mass lacks acute angles at lung interface on PA CXR
action: Inspect lateral CXR for posterior location relative to cardiac silhouette and spine; obtuse angles + posterior position strongly favor extrapulmonary benign tumor (e.g., schwannoma)
limitation: Unreliable if breast tissue or poor inspiration obscures posterior structures; does not distinguish schwannoma from other posterior neurogenic tumors

condition: When unilateral lung opacification shows air bronchograms extending from apex to base on PA CXR and lateral view confirms anterior–posterior involvement without volume loss
action: Inspect for continuity of opacification across all three lobes and absence of silhouetting of hemidiaphragm or hilum that would suggest lobar collapse; confirm no tracheal deviation
limitation: Fails if overpenetration masks subtle air bronchograms or if prior surgery/atelectasis confounds lobar boundaries

condition: When a unilateral pleural-based mass is seen on PA CXR in an asymptomatic patient without asbestos exposure
action: Inspect the mass–thoracic wall angle: obtuse (>90°) favors benign solitary fibrous tumor; acute (<90°) raises concern for mesothelioma or sarcoma. Confirm absence of mediastinal shift or volume loss.
limitation: Requires adequate inspiratory effort and centering; unreliable if mass is obscured by cardiac or diaphragmatic shadow

condition: When assessing for neuroblastic tumor recurrence on CXR and the clinical concern is subclavicular or paravertebral region
action: Inspect the paravertebral stripe bilaterally for new soft-tissue density with stippled or coarse calcifications; compare to prior studies if available
limitation: Calcifications may be invisible on CXR if <2 mm or obscured by overlying structures; CT required for confirmation

condition: When unilateral hyperlucency is present without obvious pleural line or mediastinal shift, and lung size appears reduced
action: Inspect ipsilateral intercostal space width and hemidiaphragm position relative to contralateral side; reduced spacing + elevated diaphragm supports volume loss (e.g., Swyer-James), not hyperinflation or pneumothorax
limitation: Unreliable if inspiration inadequate or diaphragm obscured by gastric air; requires comparison to contralateral side

condition: When unilateral hemithorax opacity with mediastinal shift lacks volume loss signs (normal diaphragm level, normal rib spacing) and bronchovascular markings are completely absent
action: Inspect for congenital absence: confirm absence of right main bronchus on CT or bronchoscopy; consider agenesis over atelectasis
limitation: Rare in elderly; requires cross-sectional imaging for confirmation; cannot be diagnosed by CXR alone

condition: When difficult intubation is reported and lateral neck CXR is available
action: Inspect for radiopaque material in the oropharynx (anterior to C3–C4, superior to vocal cords); if present, prioritize foreign body over pleural pathology
limitation: Fails if foreign body is radiolucent or obscured by dental hardware; requires adequate lateral projection

condition: When CXR shows bilateral nodular opacities and hilar fullness, and symmetry is ambiguous on PA view
action: Inspect lateral CXR for symmetrical anterior mediastinal lymphadenopathy (prevascular nodes) and compare hilar silhouette width left vs. right on PA; exclude unilateral volume loss or pleural effusion
limitation: Requires lateral view; unreliable if patient rotation or poor inspiration distorts hilar appearance

condition: When bilateral symmetric coarse nodular opacities improve dramatically after immunosuppression (e.g., steroids), and cavitary or fibrotic features are absent
action: Inspect for preservation of lung volumes and absence of traction bronchiectasis or reticulation on follow-up to distinguish acute hemorrhage resolution from chronic granulomatous/fibrotic disease regression
limitation: Requires adequate inspiration and comparable projection; unreliable if follow-up is CT misinterpreted as CXR

condition: When CXR shows unilateral volume loss with mediastinal shift and contralateral hyperlucency but no pleural line or effusion signs
action: Inspect axial CT at carina level for presence/absence of ipsilateral main pulmonary artery; absence confirms agenesis
limitation: Not applicable if only CXR available; requires contrast-enhanced CT for reliable vessel visualization

condition: When CXR shows a new or enlarging cavitary lesion in the upper lobe with irregular thick wall (>15 mm) and adjacent soft-tissue opacity, and symptoms are subacute
action: Inspect for mass effect (mediastinal shift, hilum displacement), wall thickness on magnified view, and absence of satellite nodules; consider malignancy over TB
limitation: Unreliable if image quality poor or no prior imaging for comparison

condition: When CXR shows diffuse interstitial opacities and fissural thickening in a patient with systemic symptoms, and cardiac silhouette appears borderline enlarged on PA view
action: Quantify cardiothoracic ratio (max transverse cardiac width / inner thoracic diameter); if ≥0.52, consider cardiomegaly and evaluate for pulmonary vascular redistribution or right heart enlargement signs
limitation: Inadequate inspiration inflates CT ratio; scoliosis distorts measurements

condition: When a right-sided lower lung opacity merges with the right heart border on PA CXR and the right costophrenic angle appears blunted anteriorly
action: Inspect lateral CXR for anterior-inferior opacity overlapping the cardiac silhouette and diaphragm dome; if present, localize to right lower lobe abutting heart and diaphragm
limitation: Unreliable if lateral view is rotated or overpenetrated; does not distinguish tumor from consolidation without clinical context

condition: When CXR shows widened mediastinum and cardiomegaly in a hemodynamically unstable patient, and aortic calcification is visible
action: Measure distance between inner and outer aortic calcific lines on PA view; >1 cm suggests intimal disruption (PAU or chronic dissection)
limitation: Requires visible aortic calcification; unreliable in young patients or non-calcified aorta

condition: When mediastinal lymphadenopathy and tracheal deviation worsen on CXR *after* ART initiation in an HIV+ patient
action: Inspect serial CXRs for interval increase in mediastinal opacity width (>1 cm) and direction of tracheal shift (away from enlarged nodes); correlate with ART start date if available
limitation: Requires at least two temporally spaced CXRs; unreliable if poor technique or non-standard projection

condition: When a well-defined, round, non-cavitating parenchymal opacity is seen in the lower lobe of an adult with acute respiratory symptoms but no air-fluid level on lateral CXR
action: Inspect for smooth, thin wall and absence of perilesional consolidation; consider hydatid cyst especially if endemic exposure possible
limitation: Cannot exclude early abscess or tumor without CT; acute symptoms reduce likelihood but do not rule out hydatid rupture

condition: When bilateral micronodules are stable over years on CXR and granulomatous disease is considered, but no hilar adenopathy or upper-lobe predominance is seen
action: Inspect CT for airway-centered nodules, mosaic attenuation, and absence of calcified granulomas; if CT unavailable, prioritize clinical symptoms (chronic cough/wheeze) and serum chromogranin A
limitation: CXR alone cannot confirm DIPNECH; rule not applicable if CT shows classic sarcoid or TB pattern
